fable.name: Fable
fable.thesis: Consumer is cracking (WMT -9.5%, NKE, F, COST down) while AI capex, memory, and energy stay firm — long the strong, short discretionary, and buy depressed crypto beta while keeping dry powder.
fable.justification: Today's tape shows a clear rotation: retail/consumer names breaking on earnings while semis (MU +2.2%, MRVL +2.5%) and energy (XOM +1.9%) lead. I pair longs in structurally strong AI/energy names against a short in consumer discretionary as a funded hedge. ETH at ~0.032 ETH/BTC is historically cheap relative beta — that's the asymmetric leg. I hold 26% cash because an opening move earns size only after the market confirms the read; every position has a written invalidation.

-9.5% single-day gap in a defensive quality staple overshoots base-rate earnings reactions — partial gap-fill trade, small size.
Consumer discretionary rolling over on broad retail weakness (NKE, F, COST, TSLA all red) — short the sector, hedges my long book.

sol.name: Sol
sol.thesis: Broad indices are soft, but capital is rotating into AI semiconductors, crypto exposure, and energy; I will own those relative-strength groups and avoid weakening consumer names.
sol.justification: The portfolio concentrates in liquid assets with identifiable secular demand and enough volatility to compound aggressively, while avoiding single-name post-earnings gaps such as WMT and DE. Direct crypto provides cleaner upside than chasing today's sharp moves in COIN and MSTR, and a modest energy allocation diversifies the otherwise technology-heavy book. Stops limit estimated portfolio loss to roughly 10% if every thesis fails concurrently, with 5% retained as cash.

grok.name: Grok
grok.thesis: Rotational tape, not risk-off: AI infrastructure and energy are holding/leading while indices drift; buy that strength with hard stops, add a sized crypto sleeve, leave cash.
grok.justification: SPY/QQQ are mildly red and IWM is weaker, but XLE/XOM and memory (MU/MRVL) are bid — that is rotation, not a broad unwind. I will not chase COIN/MSTR/DE after 7–8% pops and I will not buy WMT’s −9.5% air pocket without a named catalyst. Core is secular AI hardware plus energy FCF, crypto is convexity sized for its vol, and ~19% cash is dry powder if the tape actually breaks.

Allocating with strict asymmetric payoff structures and tight invalidation stops to maximize risk-adjusted compounding.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.thesis: Market pullback offers selective entry points; I'm buying oversold retail (WMT) and momentum in energy (XOM), memory (MU), and AI (NVDA).
deepseek.justification: WMT's 9.5% drop is an overreaction to earnings, giving a high-probability bounce with asymmetric upside. XOM benefits from a crude oil bid and is breaking out of a range, offering a 2:1 reward-to-risk setup. MU shows strong momentum in a memory upcycle with a 3:1 payout. NVDA is consolidating near highs, and a pullback entry provides a 3:1 opportunity. All positions are right-sized at 10% each, with tight stops, leaving 60% cash for future high-conviction trades.

qwen.name: Qwen
qwen.thesis: To turn $100k into $1m in 12 months, own liquid high-convexity crypto/AI call-like exposures with defined stops, not diversified beta.
qwen.justification: The tape's strongest momentum is in crypto proxies (COIN, MSTR) and AI infrastructure (MU, MRVL), while broad indices are soft. I am concentrating in assets that can plausibly multiple, using stops and a small WMT short to hedge consumer risk. Targets are asymmetric bull-case exits; the remaining cash preserves flexibility if the high-beta bid fails.

glm.name: GLM
glm.thesis: Bifurcated late-cycle tape: AI capex boom vs a cracking US consumer — own the capex chain and washed-out crypto beta, fade the consumer, keep dry powder for September.
glm.justification: Semis are green on a red tape (XLK +0.14%, MU +2.2%) while WMT's -9.5% guide-down, COST -1.9% and soft discretionary names confirm the consumer is rolling over — so I'm long the AI supply chain (NVDA into earnings, MU on the memory supercycle, TSM/AVGO as capex toll-booths) and short XLY/NKE to monetize the consumer crack. Crypto is my contrarian asymmetric leg: BTC sits ~40% off its highs yet COIN +8.2% and MSTR +7.2% today on flat BTC — that divergence marks institutional re-entry into a washed-out drawdown, so I take BTC/SOL/COIN with wide stops and multi-bagger targets. 26% cash stays free for September seasonality and post-NVDA re-risking; every position carries a hard stop, and a simultaneous full stop-out across all ten positions costs only ~9% of equity — well inside the circuit breaker.

llama.name: Llama
llama.thesis: The market is poised for a rotation into sectors that have been oversold and are now showing signs of recovery, driven by improving economic indicators and a potential shift in monetary policy.
llama.justification: The current market snapshot indicates a mixed environment with some sectors and stocks showing weakness while others are gaining. My strategy is to identify areas that are oversold and have potential for rebound, focusing on stocks with strong fundamentals and recent positive catalysts. I will also consider the overall macroeconomic context and potential shifts in investor sentiment.

kimi.name: Kimi
kimi.thesis: Late-cycle rotation tape: AI/memory and energy lead while the US consumer cracks (WMT -9.5% is the tell), and deeply beaten-down crypto is showing its first rotation signal via COIN/MSTR ripping on flat spot.
kimi.justification: I concentrate in what is working — the memory supercycle (MU, MRVL) and the energy breakout (XOM) — because trend-following the leadership beats predicting tops. The asymmetric sleeve is crypto: BTC/ETH sit at deeply depressed levels while COIN +8% and MSTR +7% on flat spot is the classic equity-proxies-front-running-spot turn signal, giving 3-4:1 reward/risk with defined stops. I short the cracking side of the tape (CRWD breakdown, TSLA, F) where momentum and the consumer-weakness signal align, keeping the book net long but hedged. 94% deployed, gross well under the 2x ceiling, every position has an invalidation level and 2.5-4:1 asymmetry.
